Description:
For entity name comparisons that score between 0.7 and 0.85 on fuzzy matching — confident enough to be worth checking but not confident enough to auto-flag — send both names to an LLM with a structured yes/no prompt to determine if they refer to the same organization. Matches above 0.85 skip the LLM entirely. Matches below 0.7 are discarded without an LLM call. This keeps API costs minimal while handling the hard cases automatically. Google LLM will be used

*Acceptance criteria:*

* {{resolveEntities(nameA, nameB, fuzzyScore)}} is a named exported async function in {{/utils/entityNorm.js}}
* If {{fuzzyScore >= 0.85}} function returns {{true}} immediately — no LLM call made
* If {{fuzzyScore < 0.7}} function returns {{false}} immediately — no LLM call made
* If {{fuzzyScore}} is between 0.7 and 0.85 an LLM API call is made with a structured prompt asking only whether the two names refer to the same organization
* LLM prompt instructs the model to respond with JSON only: {{{ "match": true }}} or {{{ "match": false }}} — no other text
* Response is parsed and the boolean value returned
* If the LLM API call fails or times out, function falls back to returning {{true}} if score >= 0.80, {{false}} if below — never throws
* LLM API key stored in {{.env}} as {{LLM_API_KEY}} — never committed to repo
* Unit tests cover: above 0.85 (no LLM call), below 0.7 (no LLM call), between thresholds with mocked LLM returning true, between thresholds with mocked LLM returning false, and LLM timeout fallback behavior
* Estimated cost per 1000 entity comparisons logged to console in development mode so the team can monitor usage
